Month by month
Reading this table: Revenue (1 Day) and Revenue (7 Days) are Meta's own reported conversion value under 1-day-click and 7-day-click attribution windows respectively; ROAS is that revenue ÷ Meta spend. Google Revenue is Google's own reported conversion value; where a given month's Google export didn't include it, that month (and any Quarterly/FY total that depends on it) shows — rather than a number that's silently missing Google's share. ASR (ad-spend ratio) is (Meta + Google spend) ÷ Shopify net sales for that period — unaffected by Google Revenue, which is shown for reference only. A row tagged till DD/MM/YY is still in progress through that date, not a complete period — any Quarterly/FY row that includes one is itself only partial too, understating that period's true total. A row also tagged from hourly is the current in-progress month, kept live every refresh from the same hourly Meta/Google/Shopify files as the Hourly & Daily Trend tabs (all-placements, includes Instagram spend) rather than waiting on a manual monthly Meta export — so its Meta Spend isn't directly comparable to older, finalized months' no-insta figures; it becomes a normal finalized row once that month's manual export supersedes it. The small figure next to each number is that metric's change vs. the prior month (MoM): green/up is favorable and red/down is unfavorable for that metric — spend and ASR are colored inverted (a rise is unfavorable), revenue and ROAS are colored normally (a rise is favorable). ASR's delta is shown as a percentage-point difference, not a relative percent. Google Revenue is shown as reported by Google — it's known to run inflated versus Shopify's numbers, which is why ASR and all "exact" reporting are based on Shopify net sales instead.

Reading this table: ROAS, ASC Rev and ASC Spends use Meta's 1-day-click attribution window throughout, matching Purchases conversion value [1-day click all conversions] and Purchases [1-day click all conversions] — not the broader window Meta may show elsewhere. CPM, CTR and LPV use raw Impressions/Link clicks/Landing page views (not attribution-windowed). Rows go through the latest complete day; a day still in progress appears once it's complete through 11PM. CPM, CTR, LPV, CVR and AOV show — where the source has no engagement data for that campaign-day (see the data-gap note for August).
